text:
emma: quick report — onboarding Kotlin sample shows duplicate refresh and stalled progress when uploading ~15MB images on some Pixel devices. repro on Pixel 6 / Android 13.

raj (sdk): duplicate refreshes meaning multiple concurrent token refresh HTTPs?

emma: yes, two refresh calls in short succession and sometimes the UI stops receiving progress for 1-3s while refresh happens. users notice jank.

carol (android): are you using Authenticator to refresh or doing app-level refresh?

emma: Authenticator returns a new Request with refreshed header (synchronous refresh using same Retrofit client). we also have app-level retry that will restart upload after a short backoff if progress stalls.

raj (sdk): that's two competing retry systems. Authenticator runs inside OkHttp internals on network threads; if it blocks for socket/connection it can cause callback ordering to shift. app retry seeing no progress may start a second upload.

sam (qa): observable sequence: upload starts -> 401 -> Authenticator blocks to refresh -> progress callbacks stop -> app retry kicks in -> second upload starts. server sometimes stores two objects.

carol (android): streaming RequestBody in sample uses `Okio.source(file)` and writes chunks in a loop. we don't close source on cancel currently.

raj (sdk): immediate mitigation options: 1) switch Authenticator to return null so 401 surfaces and app can coalesce refreshes where you control concurrency. 2) or, make refresh use a separate OkHttpClient with a small dedicated ConnectionPool so it won't compete for upload sockets. 3) make RequestBody cooperative about cancellation and close source from cancel path.

emma: can you sketch the auth-client snippet?

raj (sdk): sure: `OkHttpClient authClient = new OkHttpClient.Builder().connectionPool(new ConnectionPool(2,5,TimeUnit.MINUTES)).dispatcher(new Dispatcher(Executors.newCachedThreadPool())).build();` then construct a Retrofit instance with that client and call it from Authenticator. keeps sockets separate.

carol (android): for the cooperative RequestBody we add an AtomicBoolean `cancelled` and check it between reads; also close the Source from UI cancel handler. sample: `try (Source s = Okio.source(f)) { while ((r = s.read(buf,8192)) != -1) { if (cancelled.get()) throw new IOException("cancelled"); sink.write(buf, r); } }`

raj (sdk): and coroutines note: if using suspendCancellableCoroutine, make sure invokeOnCancellation closes the source and calls `call.cancel()` and `call.timeout().cancel()` to interrupt blocking IO where supported. we'll update the Kotlin adapter README.

sam (qa): i'll add a test case: start upload, simulate 401 from mock server, delay refresh, assert app doesn't start second upload and progress resumes once token refreshed.

emma: one more oddity — sometimes we got `SocketException: Connection reset` right after refresh then progress gap. raj any idea?

raj (sdk): likely the refresh took a socket from the pool, exhausted available streams, and when OkHttp tried to retry or hand off it led to connection reset. Using authClient or coalescing should avoid that. Also ensure you aren't using `postAtFrontOfQueue` for progress updates; switch to `post()` and coalesce small updates.

carol (android): will patch sample to: move auth header injection to app-level coalescer (Authenticator returns null), add `CancellableStreamingRequestBody`, and include auth-only client example as an alternative. will open PR and include small emu CI test.

ci-bot: queued pipeline for branch fix/auth-coalesce-230123. e2e tests scheduled.

emma: thanks all — will follow up with logs and a tiny repro app. :party_parrot:
